title: The Concept of Wave-Particle Duality
text:
Wave-particle duality posits that every quantum entity, such as photons or electrons, exhibits both wave-like and particle-like characteristics. This means that these entities are not strictly confined to one nature but display properties of both depending on the experimental conditions used for measurement.

The double-slit experiment provides compelling evidence for this duality. When observed through two slits, individual particles initially behave as if they passed through both slits simultaneously, creating an interference pattern characteristic of waves. However, when detectors are placed at the slits to measure which path the particle takes, the wave behavior collapses, and only localized, predictable particle impacts are recorded.

This paradoxical nature challenges classical intuitions about reality, suggesting that measurement itself plays a fundamental role in defining physical properties at the quantum scale.
